final_decision.rationale: 1) JPEG: block_boundary 3.20/1.76/1.53 in all three supports (0% FP signal) + dct_zero_ratio 0.93 -> JPEG confirmed; unique_G=256 rules out quantization. 2) Global: variance_ratio 2.52/2.34/2.01 with only 2.1%/12.3%/15.8% clipped and mixed-sign mean_shift (-29/+16/+2). Mixed sign is impossible for a fixed gamma/brightness; LUT scale variant (contrast_strengthen_scale) produced 16% extreme pixels vs target 2.1% -> ruled out. Logistic contrast_strengthen_stretch maps per-channel means toward 0.5, explains mixed signs and low clipping. 3) Severity scan at jpeg:5 on pair0: stretch c=6/8/10 -> 23.98/31.07/24.65 dB; at stretch:4: jpeg q18/q12/q8/q5 -> 26.07/25.93/26.09/31.07 dB. Peak is sharp at stretch:4 + jpeg:5, CI 10/10 with all content-independent diffs <=3% (block_boundary 2%, unique 0%, zero_crossing 2%). 4) Order: stretch->JPEG (31.07) beats JPEG->stretch (25.16, unique_R 134 vs target 256; a final pointwise map cannot regenerate unique values). 5) Rejected 3rd steps: saturate_weaken_HSV:1 (28.23) and blur_gaussian:1 (28.32) both lowered PSNR; 2 consecutive no-improvement rounds -> stop. 6) Cross-support verification with the same pipeline: pair1 28.27 dB CI 10/10, pair2 26.13 dB CI 10/10. Residual PSNR 26-31 dB (not infinite) attributed to small tone-curve/JPEG-quantization sensitivity differences; no parameter combination reached >31.07 within the 17-test budget.

Content-dependent clipping; pair0 clips only 2.1% while pair1/2 clip 12-16%. This pattern matters for subtype: PIL contrast_strengthen_scale preserves the image mean and can only shift it via hard clipping, which on pair0 (bright content, mean_shift -29.0) would require ~16% clipped pixels (R0 measured 16% extremes) vs target 2.1%. signal_reinterpretation.reassessment: Mixed sign across supports. Fixed monotone tone curves (gamma/brightness, all 8 brightness_* variants) shift all image means in one direction and are impossible. contrast_strengthen_stretch normalizes each channel by its own mean, so the output channel mean lands near 0.5*255 and the shift sign depends on the clean image's brightness -> mixed signs are the expected signature, not an anomaly.

This does not indicate an additional gamma step. New idea: a priority-0 brightness step BEFORE the mean-normalizing stretch would be hidden in mean_shift but would reshape the curve; tested both gamma directions (H1) -> 23.21/25.54 dB, both worse.

reflection_R1.decision_rationale: Fresh full analysis reproduced every R0 step verdict. Five new signal-driven candidates (global control, pre-stretch brightness gamma both directions, saturation strengthen, matched-severity scale subtype) all failed: best R1 pair0 PSNR = 25.54 dB vs R0 31.07 dB, so neither >40 dB nor +2 dB was reached. The retained pipeline's per-step signals are all consistent (JPEG 0%FP, stretch mean-normalization explains mixed-sign mean shifts, no producible noise/blur). Two reinterpretation rounds without improvement -> protocol termination; R0 pipeline retained unchanged.
limits: k=3 support pairs (0469/0353/0313); pair0 is primary and all new candidates were screened on pair0 because none came within 5 dB of the R0 baseline.
x_distortion severities are integers 1-5; a true non-integer tone-curve/JPEG parameter would make the simulation plateau at 26-31 dB. This is library-resolution mismatch, not a missing degradation.
support PSNR 19.70 is compatible with the 2.1-15.8% clipped pixels (information loss) plus small support; it is not by itself evidence of a missing step.
